title: Law justifies the worker by debt, never the sinner—even if penitent
source_text: XXXIII. Itaque lex justificat non credentem, sed operantem, idque secundum debitum, non secundum gratiam. Nec enim lex rigide accepta ulli gratiam facit, aut promittit, sed unicuique severe denunciat quod illi ex stricto jure debetur. Ac proinde nullum impium & peccatorem justificat; quantumvis supponatur poenitentia ductus redire ad meliorem frugem. Adeoque cum omnes homines & in peccato nati, & multi peccatores sint, nullus omnino potest ex legis operibus, & per legem justificari.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the law justifies not the believer but the worker—and that according to debt, not according to grace. For the law rigidly taken grants or promises grace to no one, but severely denounces to each what is due him by strict right. And so it justifies no ungodly person and sinner—however much he is supposed, led by repentance, to return to better fruit. And since all people are both born in sin and many are sinners, no one at all can be justified from works of the law and through the law.
pass_b_english: Law justifies only the perfect worker by debt—never the sinner by grace.
Born in sin, no one can be justified by law-works.

lemmas.gloss: according to debt, not according to grace

choices.english: the law [justifies] the one who works
choices.why: Legal justification is debt-wages, not grace.
